_doc: Market Revolution / transportation growth data. Coordinates [lon, lat]. A line without `reached` draws in when the year passes `opened`. A line with `reached` grows waypoint by waypoint: each entry = the year construction reached waypoint index `wp` (first entry = start of construction, nothing drawn yet). Routes run through real towns but are simplified centre lines (approximate: true). Fractional years: 1869.36 ≈ May 10, 1869.

lines.name: Erie Canal
lines.note: Opened Oct. 26, 1825 (the Seneca Chief left Buffalo for Albany and New York). 363 miles, Buffalo to Albany, following the Mohawk Valley east of Rome. Sections opened from 1819; drawn here at full opening.
lines.source: New York State Canal Corporation, 'Erie Canal history'; Erie Canalway National Heritage Corridor (NPS). Route approximate (town to town).

lines.name: National Road
lines.note: Begun at Cumberland, Md., 1811; reached Wheeling 1818; Zanesville c. 1830; Columbus 1833; graded (partly unfinished) to Vandalia, Ill., by c. 1839. Indiana–Illinois timing approximate.
lines.source: Federal Highway Administration, 'The National Road' (fhwa.dot.gov); National Road Heritage Corridor. Dates west of Columbus approximate.

lines.name: Baltimore & Ohio Railroad
lines.label: B&O Railroad
lines.note: First US common-carrier railroad: Ellicott's Mills May 1830, Harpers Ferry Dec. 1834, Cumberland Nov. 1842, Wheeling on the Ohio Jan. 1853.
lines.source: B&O Railroad Museum, 'History of the B&O'; Stover, History of the Baltimore and Ohio Railroad (1987). Route approximate.

lines.name: Pennsylvania Railroad
lines.label: Pennsylvania R.R.
lines.note: Harrisburg–Lewistown 1849; Altoona 1850; through service to Pittsburgh Dec. 1852 (via the Allegheny Portage RR until the Horseshoe Curve line opened Feb. 1854). Philadelphia–Harrisburg used earlier lines (Philadelphia & Columbia, 1834).
lines.source: Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission, 'Pennsylvania Railroad'; Churella, The Pennsylvania Railroad vol. 1 (2013). Route approximate.

lines.name: Buffalo–Chicago rail line
lines.label: Rails reach Chicago
lines.note: Michigan Southern reached Chicago Feb. 1852; Buffalo–Cleveland 1852 and Cleveland–Toledo 1853 completed the lake-shore route (later Lake Shore & Michigan Southern). Drawn as one line at 1852.
lines.source: Encyclopedia of Chicago (Chicago Historical Society), 'Railroads'; Cronon, Nature's Metropolis (1991). Route approximate.

lines.name: Chicago & Rock Island Railroad
lines.label: Rock Island R.R.
lines.note: First railroad to reach the Mississippi River, Feb. 22, 1854.
lines.source: Encyclopedia of Chicago, 'Railroads'; Rock Island Arsenal Museum. Route approximate.

lines.name: Illinois Central Railroad
lines.label: Illinois Central
lines.note: Chicago branch, Chicago–Centralia–Cairo; the whole system (with the Galena line) was completed Sept. 1856, built with the first federal railroad land grant (1850).
lines.source: Illinois State Historical Society; Encyclopedia of Chicago, 'Illinois Central Railroad'. Route approximate.

lines.name: Chicago & North Western (to Council Bluffs)
lines.label: Chicago & North Western
lines.note: Chicago to the Mississippi at Fulton/Clinton 1855; Cedar Rapids 1859; Council Bluffs (across from Omaha) Jan. 1867. Dates approximate.
lines.source: Encyclopedia of Chicago, 'Chicago & North Western Railway'; Iowa DOT, 'Iowa railroad history'. Route and intermediate dates approximate.

lines.name: Union Pacific Railroad
lines.label: Union Pacific
lines.note: Track-laying west from Omaha began July 1865; North Platte Dec. 1866; Cheyenne Nov. 1867; Ogden March 1869; met the Central Pacific at Promontory Summit, Utah Territory, May 10, 1869. Intermediate dates approximate.
lines.source: NPS, Golden Spike National Historical Park, 'The Race to Promontory'; Union Pacific, 'History'. Route and intermediate dates approximate.

lines.name: Central Pacific Railroad
lines.label: Central Pacific
lines.note: First rails at Sacramento Oct. 1863; Colfax 1865; through the Sierra Nevada (Summit Tunnel) to Truckee 1868; Reno May 1868; Promontory Summit May 10, 1869. Intermediate dates approximate.
lines.source: NPS, Golden Spike National Historical Park; California State Railroad Museum, 'Central Pacific Railroad'. Route and intermediate dates approximate.

cities._doc: Population of the city proper at each census (New York = Manhattan only, before the 1898 consolidation; Philadelphia before the 1854 consolidation counts the city proper only). Values between censuses are interpolated for animation only.
cities.source: U.S. Census Bureau, Gibson, 'Population of the 100 Largest Cities and Other Urban Places in the United States: 1790 to 1990', Population Division Working Paper No. 27 (1998), Tables 5–11 (1820–1880) (https://www.census.gov/library/working-papers/1998/demo/POP-twps0027.html; tables at https://www2.census.gov/library/working-papers/1998/demographics/pop-twps0027/tab05.txt … tab11.txt).

list.name: Philadelphia
list.note: Jump 1850→1860 = 1854 consolidation of Philadelphia County into the city.

list.name: St. Louis
list.note: 1830 corrected 5,852 → 4,977 per Working Paper 27 Table 6 (5,852 appears in some other compilations).

list.name: Chicago
list.note: 1833 = incorporation as a town, ≈350 residents (estimate, not a census figure; not re-verified this session). 1840–1880 values verified against WP27.
